source.title: Londonderry Sentinel, 17 January 1920, p. 5: "Waterside Electoral Area" (results table, counts 1 to 4 read from the table, and "An analysis of the voting", which gives every transfer). Candidates' names as nominated: Londonderry Sentinel, 6 January 1920, p. 3 ("Londonderry Municipal Nominations of Candidates").
source.publisher: Londonderry Sentinel (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: first preferences and counts 1-4 transcribed from the printed table; counts 5-9 from the printed account of each transfer (the sixth count's surplus of 2 "divided between the two remaining Nationalist candidates", and the seventh count's 8 votes besides Pollock's 455 fixed by Thompson's printed final surplus of 55); every count adds to the printed valid vote of 2,573 and the quota is 2,573 / 10 + 1 = 258 as printed

note: Proportional representation (single transferable vote) under the Local Government (Ireland) Act 1919; polled 15 January 1920. Counted 16 January 1920 by Sir Henry Miller, returning officer. The area returned 9 members; Anderson and Bradley, at the top of the poll, became its aldermen. Unionist electors largely voted in ballot-paper order, as advised. Thompson's surplus of 55 (ninth count) was wholly non-transferable, and Mrs Margaret Morris, the higher of the two remaining candidates, was declared elected to the last seat without reaching the quota. The table's non-transferable papers at counts 2-4 (5, 2 and 4) lay within the transferred candidates' quotas and are not shown as non-transferable votes. Party labels are the Sentinel's: its "N." covers the joint Nationalist, Sinn Féin and Labour ticket (another report calls Mrs Morris a Sinn Féin candidate).
